title: Understanding Drain Trap Seals
description: Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a properly maintained drain trap to block sewer gases from entering the living space. The fundamental principle is simple: a specific volume of water remains trapped in the bend of the pipe, acting as an airtight liquid barrier. However, issues like evaporation, induced siphonage, or back-pressure can compromise this seal if venting is inadequate. Regular inspections and proper trap priming help maintain this crucial barrier, ensuring a safe and odor-free environment for building occupants.

Understanding Drain Trap Seals

Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a properly maintained drain trap to block sewer gases from entering the living space. The fundamental principle is simple: a specific volume of water remains trapped in the bend of the pipe, acting as an airtight liquid barrier. However, issues like evaporation, induced siphonage, or back-pressure can compromise this seal if venting is inadequate. Regular inspections and proper trap priming help maintain this crucial barrier, ensuring a safe and odor-free environment for building occupants.
